target_customer: At YC: battery customers in mobility, electronics and utilities; by 2021: carbon credit buyers, then commercial and eventually individual buyers of modular carbon capture scrubbers
problem: Battery R&D is slow and custom cells take long to reach customers; the company later targeted removing CO2 from air with small electricity-driven modular units.
business_model: Early: fast custom battery development using a fabless-style model. 2021: sell carbon credits first, later sell scrubber hardware to commercial customers and consumers
product_category: Battery development, then modular direct air capture

founders.name: Nuno Pereira
founders.background_notes: From TechCrunch, August 2019: became interested in batteries through working on cars. YC page lists him as founder and CEO.

founders.name: David Pervan
founders.role: Initial executive team member (TechCrunch 2019); described as co-founder in 2021 coverage
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2019 names him with Martin Hansen as the initial executive team and notes a now-departed co-founder who is not named; the co-founder label comes from a search result summary of 2021 coverage.

technical_complexity.rationale: Combining computational battery design, chemistry and an automated manufacturing system (about 700 batteries a day claimed in 2019) is demanding; the later electrochemical carbon capture units were prototype-stage in 2021.

defensibility.rationale: The 2019 pitch relied on a systems approach and test data; the 2021 carbon capture device was in patent filing, so the moat was unproven.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action found; the company pivoted away from batteries by 2021.

market_need_then: In 2019 the company reported 14 million dollars in non-binding letters of intent from potential battery customers; by 2021 demand cited was for carbon removal credits and investor interest in climate technology.

branding.domain_note: Uses holygrail.ai; no source on how the domain was obtained.

identity.logo: A logo and a list of backers appear on the website, with no product text
identity.voice_and_tone: Mission framing of removing billions of tons of CO2 (company Medium post)

branding.community_and_virality: Press such as RESET and Springwise used the Holy Grail phrase in headlines for the carbon capture story; no merch or community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Trade and climate press (TechCrunch, CleanTechnica, Springwise) covered the company and a well-known backer list, but the name is a generic phrase and no source shows brand-driven growth.

pivots.from: Machine-learning-assisted battery R&D and custom test battery production (2019)
pivots.to: Modular direct air capture scrubbers and carbon credits
pivots.why: Not stated in the sources found; TechCrunch June 2021 covers only the carbon capture plan

outcome_analysis: Holy Grail entered YC in 2019 as a battery R&D company, then by June 2021 raised a 2.7 million seed from climate funds and notable angels to build modular carbon capture scrubbers. It remains listed as active with 7 people, but sources show no later funding, products or revenue, so the outcome is unclear.
notes: Competitor list left empty: the 2019 TechCrunch article names no competitors and a dated 2019 source for rivals such as Wildcat Discovery was not found. The seed investor list and amount come from a search summary of TechCrunch and CleanTechnica coverage (the amount also appears in the YC page headline); lead investor is conflicting across sources. A 150K YC seed in 2019 appears only in a London Tech Watch item and is not recorded. Seedtable lists Palo Alto and some sources say Mountain View while YC says San Francisco. Martin Hansen is named in the 2019 article as part of the initial executive team and not listed as a founder. Education not found. Outcome search found no acquisition, shutdown or layoffs.
